title: Login/Logout, Public Visibility Fixes, TTS PWA Fix, Admin Controls & Photo Optimization

requirements.text: Implement one-click Internet Identity login/logout: clicking the login button must immediately open the Internet Identity flow (Google/passkey) with no additional password prompt. On successful authentication the user is logged in; a logout button must be visible and functional at all times when authenticated.

quotes: One-click Login/Logout — Google/passkey पर click करते ही सीधे Internet Identity से login, कोई password नहीं
login me koe password nhi mange seedha hi login ho or logout ho gmail pr click krke

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking the login button launches Internet Identity directly without any intermediate password form
Google/passkey option is presented in the Internet Identity popup
After login, the UI shows a visible logout button
Clicking logout clears the session and returns the user to the unauthenticated state
No custom password field is rendered anywhere in the login flow

requirements.text: Fix Vrat Katha public visibility: when an admin uploads or publishes a Vrat Katha, it must immediately be visible to all public (unauthenticated) users, not only to the admin. The backend query for listing kathas must return all published/active kathas regardless of caller identity, and the frontend must display them without requiring login.

quotes: Vrat Katha public visibility fix — Upload होने के बाद सभी public users को दिखे
vrat katha upload krne ke baad public ko nahi dikh raha hai sitf admin ko visisble hai isse bhi thik kro

acceptanceCriteria: A Vrat Katha uploaded/published by admin appears in the listing for unauthenticated users immediately
The backend getKathas (or equivalent) query returns published kathas for anonymous callers
No login is required to browse or read Vrat Kathas
Admin-only drafts or pending items are still hidden from public

requirements.text: Fix Community posts public visibility: admin-approved community posts must be visible to all users, including unauthenticated/public visitors. The backend query for listing community posts must return approved posts for anonymous callers, and the Community page must render them without requiring login.

quotes: Community posts public visibility — Admin द्वारा approved posts सभी users को visible हों

acceptanceCriteria: Approved community posts are visible on the Community page to logged-out users
Backend getCommunityPosts (or equivalent) returns approved posts for anonymous callers
Pending or rejected posts remain hidden from public
Authenticated users and anonymous users see the same set of approved posts

requirements.text: Fix Narration (TTS) in PWA/installed app: the text-to-speech narration that works on the desktop browser must also work correctly when the app is installed as a PWA on mobile devices. Update the useSpeechNarration hook and any relevant pages (KathaDetail, AartiDetail, Bhajans, Mantras, Chalisa) to use a PWA-compatible TTS strategy — ensure the Speech Synthesis API is re-initialized after page visibility changes, handle the known Chrome Android PWA bug where voices are not loaded until an utterance event fires, and add a fallback resume mechanism so narration is not silently blocked.

quotes: Narration (TTS) fix — PWA/downloaded app में भी narration सही से काम करे
narration option web pr sahi kam krta hai lekin download hone ke baad nahi krta

acceptanceCriteria: TTS narration plays correctly when the app is installed and opened as a PWA on Android/iOS
Voices load properly on first use inside the PWA without requiring a page reload
Narration controls (play/pause/stop) are functional in the PWA environment
No silent failure — if TTS is unavailable an appropriate message is shown to the user

requirements.text: Implement Community Admin Control panel: the Admin Panel must include a dedicated 'Community Approval Queue' tab listing all pending community posts (text, images, videos). For each pending post the admin must be able to Accept (approve and make public), Reject (decline without publishing), or Delete (permanently remove) the post. Already-approved posts must also be deletable by the admin. Backend must expose the necessary update/delete functions restricted to admin callers.

quotes: Community Admin Control — Posts का approval queue, accept/reject/delete

acceptanceCriteria: Admin Panel has a 'Pending Posts' or 'Approval Queue' tab
Each pending post shows its content, author, and timestamp
Admin can click Accept to approve a post (it becomes visible to public)
Admin can click Reject to decline a post (it is not shown publicly)
Admin can click Delete to permanently remove any post
Non-admin users cannot access approval or delete functions
After an action, the queue updates to reflect the new state

requirements.text: Optimize Community Photos loading speed: images in community posts must load faster. Implement lazy loading for images in CommunityPostCard (use native loading='lazy' attribute), add image dimension hints to avoid layout shift, and where possible display a low-quality placeholder or skeleton while the full image loads. If images are stored as blobs in the backend, serve them efficiently; avoid re-fetching large blobs on every render by caching blob URLs.

quotes: Community Photos speed optimization — Images जल्दी load हों

acceptanceCriteria: Community post images use native lazy loading
A skeleton/placeholder is shown while images are loading
Images below the fold do not block initial page render
Blob URLs for backend-stored images are cached and not recreated on every render
Visible improvement in perceived load time for the Community page

constraints: Do not modify files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts or frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts — compose or wrap them instead
Do not modify files under frontend/src/components/ui
All Motoko logic must remain in the single backend/main.mo actor
Internet Identity is the only supported authentication method — no custom username/password backend
nonGoals: Adding any third-party OAuth outside of Internet Identity
External image CDN or cloud storage integration
Building a separate microservice for media handling
